subject: Access-trace exportability & deletion choreography — Q&A for legal/infra
messages:
From: Sanjay Pillai <sanjay.pillai@meditechcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit trail exports and deletion process

Hi Hannah —

Were working through our records retention and legal-hold needs and need clarity on two things for Meditech tenant:

1) Export windows: can we request scoped exports (tenant + user + time-range) for access/audit logs? What formats/time-to-deliver should we expect for 30/90/365 day pulls?

2) Deletion choreography: if we issue an erase request (or a legal hold is lifted), what guarantees do you provide that exported copies are removed (including cross-region caches/backups)? Is there an attestation we can get?

Wed like a short summary and an example timeline for an export + subsequent certified deletion.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Pillai
Head of Compliance, Meditech Corp
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Pillai <sanjay.pillai@meditechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exports and deletion process

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then a concise runbook we can follow:

- Scoped exports: yes — we can slice by tenant, user ID(s), event types, and date ranges. Output formats: JSONL (default) and Parquet (if you prefer columnar).
- Delivery: standard hosted exports (for tenants on our hosted plan) are typically delivered as a signed S3 URL or SFTP bundle within 48-72 hours for batches up to 30 days; larger or longer-range extracts (365d) can take 3-7 days depending on slice size.
- Retention defaults: hosted tenant audit logs are retained 30 days by default; Dedicated/Private plans can have configurable retention up to multi-year by contract.
- Deletion/attestation: deletion in the control plane (tenant-level TTL) marks records for erase and triggers purge across primary stores; for exported copies we provide a certified deletion attestation if those exports were generated via Redwoods export job (we cannot certify deletion of files that Meditech has copied off-platform). For cross-region replicas and backups we follow our erase workflow — primary purge + background wipe of replicas; we can provide timeline and a signed attestation document once complete.

Attached: export_options_matrix.pdf (matrix of formats, estimated lead times, scoping examples).

Proposed next step: if youre open to it well run a dry-run export (no PII included) to demonstrate scoping and delivery. If that looks good, well schedule a full extract and, separately, a deletion attestation job scoped to the export artifacts.

Ill loop in Karthik for the technical details of the erase pipeline and Marissa for the compliance attestation.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-09T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exports and deletion process

Hannah — quick technical clarifications to include in the customer-facing runbook. Quoting your note above for context: 

> - Scoped exports: yes — we can slice by tenant, user ID(s), event types, and date ranges.

Mechanics: we generate export slices from the immutable event stream. Exports are exported as compressed ndjson (JSONL) by default. For very large ranges we generate chunked Parquet segments with a manifest. Key constraints to call out:

- When you request a date-range crossing a snapshot boundary theres an additional 12-48h assembly step.
- TTL/deletion in the control plane flips a tombstone bit and schedules background re-writes; this means immediate reads from primary stores are blocked but low-level media (cold backups/offsite snapshots) may not be instantly purged.
- Certified deletion workflow: we run a three-step process (mark->sweep->verify). Verification includes checksums of deleted segments and a signed attestation PDF. Typical timeframe: 5-7 business days for a single-region hosted export; multi-region or legal-hold flows can extend to 10-15 business days.

Action items for the runbook: include a sample HubSpot ticket template, a list of required customer parameters (tenant id, user list, date range, delivery method), and a consent checkbox confirming Meditech will not retain copies beyond agreed terms unless explicitly allowed.

Karthik
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Pillai <sanjay.pillai@meditechcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exports and deletion process

Hi Sanjay —

Following up with an explicit, customer-ready plan so you can share with Meditechs legal team. Proposed dry-run + production flow: 

1) Dry-run export (no PII) — scope: tenant=meditech-01, users=sample set (you provide 3 user ids), dates=2026-03-01 to 2026-03-31. Delivery: signed S3 URL. ETA: 48hr.
2) Review & sign-off by Meditech (you verify scope/format).
3) Production export — full slice as scoped. ETA: 3-5 business days depending on size. Delivery options: S3 signed URLs (preferred), SFTP, or transfer via our secure transfer service.
4) If and when you request deletion of the exported artifacts that were generated by Redwood export job, Redwood will run the certified deletion workflow (mark->sweep->verify) and provide a signed attestation including checksums and timestamps. Expected attestation timeline: 5-7 business days for single-region hosted.

Please confirm: preferred dry-run date window and your delivery preference (S3 vs SFTP). Also let us know if the legal team requires the attestation to reference a contract clause or a particular PO/HSB id.

Attached: export_dryrun_checklist.txt (simple checklist well use to kick the job).

Thanks — happy to schedule a short call if that helps.

— Hannah
From: Sanjay Pillai <sanjay.pillai@meditechcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit trail exports and deletion process

Thanks Hannah (and team) — that is helpful. Wed like to proceed with the dry-run:

- Dry-run scope: 3 user IDs (Ill send in a separate email), dates: 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-31.
- Delivery: S3 signed URL.
- For the attestation: our legal team wants the signed deletion attestation to reference our contract number (MED-2025-77).

Also could you include a copy of your SOC 2 / security evidence that covers export and deletion controls? If you can attach or point us to the evidence bundle that would speed legal review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Sanjay
